candidate_relations.reason: The oropharyngeal antigen exceeded 5000 pg/mL, establishing COVID-19, but the label omits the fatal myocardial injury and diffuse necrosis.
Positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen, elevated troponin, and absent coronary stenosis support COVID-associated myocardial injury, but the diffuse contraction-band necrosis is not specified.
Histology showed diffuse contraction-band necrosis with only several lymphocytes, insufficient for classic lymphocytic myocarditis.
Thrombopenia and platelet microaggregates were present, but no hemolytic anemia, schistocytes, or systemic TTP syndrome is reported.

Although contraction-band necrosis can accompany catecholamine injury, the record attributes the damage to acute COVID with inflammatory cytokines and microvascular platelet aggregation rather than stress cardiomyopathy.
